title: smtp: sieve_client.rs — Unix socket HTTP client + header fallback
description:
Implement the two halves of sieve_client.rs: daemon client and header-based fallback.

What: crates/smtp/src/sieve_client.rs (new file)

Part A — Daemon client:
  pub async fn eval_via_daemon(
      cfg: &SieveDaemonConfig,
      script_bytes: &[u8],
      raw_message: &[u8],
      envelope_from: &str,
      envelope_to: &str,
  ) -> Result<Vec<SieveAction>, SieveClientError>
  
  Algorithm:
  1. Build hyper client with custom connector: UnixConnector wraps tokio::net::UnixStream::connect(socket_path). Use hyper-util (already in dep tree via axum) or implement connector directly.
  2. Base64-encode script and message; serialize to JSON.
  3. POST to http://localhost/filter via the Unix connector (authority is ignored, all requests go to the socket).
  4. Apply connect_timeout_ms and request_timeout_ms via tokio::time::timeout.
  5. Deserialize response; map JSON action objects to Vec<SieveAction>.
  6. On connection error / timeout: return Err(SieveClientError::Unreachable).

  pub async fn check_via_daemon(cfg: &SieveDaemonConfig, script_bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), String>
  — Same connector; POST /check; 200→Ok(()); 422→Err(error string).

Part B — Header fallback:
  pub fn fallback_routing(raw_message: &[u8]) -> Vec<SieveAction>
  
  Algorithm:
  1. Scan raw_message bytes line by line (stop at first blank line = end of headers).
  2. Collect header values for (case-insensitive): Newsgroups, List-ID, X-List-ID, X-Listid, X-List-Id.
  3. Priority: if Newsgroups present, split on ',' trim whitespace → FileInto("newsgroup:{name}") for each.
  4. Else if any List-* header present, take first non-empty:
     - Extract content inside <...> if angle brackets present; else use raw value.
     - Normalize: trim, lowercase, replace any char not in [a-z0-9.-] with '.', collapse runs of '.'.
     - Return [FileInto("newsgroup:{normalized}")].
  5. If nothing found: return [Keep].
  
  SieveClientError enum: Unreachable, Timeout, Protocol(String).

Defensive rules:
- Never log message content or envelope addresses at INFO level; only count/metric at DEBUG.
- Treat all input bytes as untrusted; do not parse beyond the header section.
- Fallback must be infallible (no I/O, no unwrap that can fail).
